questions.enonce_markdown:
An organic compound W, on analysis was found to have a relative molecular mass of 58 and an empirical formula $\mathrm{C_3H_6O}$.

(i) Define Relative molecular mass.

(ii) What information can be obtained from the mass spectrum of the compound?

Determine

A: The molecular formula of W

B: Suggest two possible structures of W *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The **relative molecular mass** ($M_r$) of a substance is the weighted average mass of one molecule of the substance compared with one twelfth of the mass of one atom of carbon-12 (it has no units).

**(ii)** From the mass spectrum of a compound one obtains:

- the **relative molecular mass**: the peak of highest $m/z$ (the molecular ion peak, $M^+$) gives $M_r$ (here $m/z = 58$);
- **structural information** from the fragmentation pattern: the $m/z$ values of the fragment ions identify the pieces of the molecule (for example a peak at 29 for $\mathrm{CHO^+}$ or $\mathrm{C_2H_5^+}$, at 43 for $\mathrm{CH_3CO^+}$), which helps to identify the functional groups and the structure;
- the **relative abundance of isotopes** (from the $M+1$ and $M+2$ peaks, for example the number of carbon atoms, or the presence of Cl or Br).

**A. Molecular formula.** Empirical formula mass of $\mathrm{C_3H_6O}$: $3(12) + 6(1) + 16 = 58$.

$$n = \frac{M_r}{\text{empirical formula mass}} = \frac{58}{58} = 1$$

The molecular formula is the same as the empirical formula: **$\mathrm{C_3H_6O}$**.

**B. Two possible structures** (isomers of $\mathrm{C_3H_6O}$ containing $\mathrm{C{=}O}$):

- **Propanal**, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}$ (an aldehyde);
- **Propanone**, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$ (a ketone).

(Other isomers also fit the formula, for example prop-2-en-1-ol, $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CHCH_2OH}$, but the carbonyl compounds are the expected answer.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) A liquid X with less than 4 carbon atoms was subjected to the following tests in the laboratory. Complete the table below by giving the corresponding inferences.

| Test | Reagent | Observation | Inferences |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | PCl$_5$ | No white fumes | |
| B | Bromine water | No reaction | |
| C | 2,4- dinitrophenyl hydrazine | Orange precipitate | |
| D | Ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollen's Reagent) | No reaction | |

(ii) Suggest an identity for compound X. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)**

| Test | Reagent | Observation | Inference |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ | No white fumes | **No $-\mathrm{OH}$ group**: not an alcohol or carboxylic acid (these give steamy white fumes of $\mathrm{HCl}$) |
| B | Bromine water | No reaction | **No $\mathrm{C{=}C}$** (the compound is saturated, with no alkene group; it is not a phenol or an arylamine either) |
| C | 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine | Orange precipitate | **A carbonyl group, $\mathrm{C{=}O}$, is present** (aldehyde or ketone): the 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone is formed |
| D | Tollens' reagent | No reaction | **Not an aldehyde** (no silver mirror), so the carbonyl compound is a **ketone** |

**(ii)** X is a ketone with fewer than 4 carbon atoms. The only such ketone is **propanone**, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$ (the next ketone, butanone, has 4 carbon atoms). Methanal, ethanal and propanal are aldehydes and would give a silver mirror.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the systematic name for each of the following compounds.

(i) $\mathrm{CH_3CH(CH_3)CH_2NH_2}$

(ii) $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2COCl}$ *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** $\mathrm{CH_3CH(CH_3)CH_2NH_2}$: the longest chain containing the carbon bonded to nitrogen has 3 carbons (propane), with the $\mathrm{NH_2}$ on carbon 1 and a methyl group on carbon 2: **2-methylpropan-1-amine** (also called 2-methylpropylamine or isobutylamine).

**(ii)** $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2COCl}$: an acyl chloride with 4 carbons including the carbonyl carbon (butane chain): **butanoyl chloride**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State the reagents and reaction conditions for the conversions in the table below.

| | Reaction | Reagent | Reaction condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| i | $\mathrm{C_6H_6} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_6NO_2}$ | | |
| ii | $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$ | | |
| iii | $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2CN} + \mathrm{KCl}$ | | |

*[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| | Reaction | Reagent | Reaction condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| i | $\mathrm{C_6H_6} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2}$ (nitration of benzene) | **concentrated nitric acid and concentrated sulphuric acid** (nitrating mixture) | warm at about $50$ to $55^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (not above $55^\circ\mathrm{C}$, to avoid dinitration) |
| ii | $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$ (dehydration) | **concentrated sulphuric acid** (in excess) | heat to about $170^\circ\mathrm{C}$ |
| iii | $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2CN} + \mathrm{KCl}$ (nucleophilic substitution) | **potassium cyanide, KCN, dissolved in ethanol** | heat under reflux |

Equations: (i) $\mathrm{C_6H_6} + \mathrm{HNO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$ (the electrophile is $\mathrm{NO_2^+}$ formed in $\mathrm{HNO_3} + 2\mathrm{H_2SO_4} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NO_2^+} + \mathrm{H_3O^+} + 2\mathrm{HSO_4^-}$). (ii) Alternative: pass the ethanol vapour over heated aluminium oxide, $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$, at about $300$ to $350^\circ\mathrm{C}$. (iii) The product is propanenitrile; the carbon chain is lengthened by one carbon.
